name: axross
title: axross files (a folder and your SFTP connections)
description: axross's file tools (axross-headless-mcp 0.15.180, the user's own project; the modules this server runs reviewed, the rest of the package not in the image) on the folder mounted at /work and, with remote_open, on the SFTP connections saved as axross profiles: list_dir, stat, read_file (text or base64, at most 4 MiB a call, with offsets), checksum, search, walk, recursive_checksum, grep (regex in a killable child process, 5 s a file), list_versions, open_version_read; remote_profiles (the saved profiles, no secret), remote_open, remote_close, list_backends. Only with AXROSS_WRITE=1: write_file (atomic), mkdir, remove, rename, copy, bulk_copy, symlink, hardlink, chmod (no setuid, setgid, sticky or group/world write). On /work every path stays beneath the folder: '..', absolute paths and symlinks out of it are refused, every open is made beneath the folder's descriptor without following a link (openat2), and secret files (SSH and GnuPG keys, .env, credentials, tokens, any file holding a private key) are never read. A remote path is the SSH account's, as the server allows it (--mcp-root does not apply there); '..' is refused for writes and a profile flagged production stays read-only. SFTP profiles only (no other backend, no proxy, no ProxyCommand, no SSH agent); host keys only from known_hosts (an unknown one is refused, never trusted on first use); passwords only from AXROSS_PASSWORDS. No scripts, no remote commands, no agent, no HTTP transport.

env.name: AXROSS_WRITE
env.description: 1: the write tools are offered (write_file, mkdir, remove, rename, copy, bulk_copy, symlink, hardlink, chmod); without it the server only reads

env.name: AXROSS_PASSWORDS
env.description: The stored passwords of your profiles as JSON, {"PROFILE": "password"} ("PROFILE:proxy" for a proxy's): read once, never written or shown

env.name: AXROSS_MCP_REMOTE_TIMEOUT
env.description: Seconds an SFTP request may go unanswered, 5-3600 (default 60)

mounts.description: The folder the file tools work on, read-only (--mount /work=DIR:ro; :rw with AXROSS_WRITE=1 to change it); without it an empty folder
axross's config folder, read-only (--mount /axross=~/.config/axross:ro): only its profiles.json is read, never written
known_hosts and the key files your profiles name, read-only (--mount /ssh=~/.ssh:ro); a key file is looked up here by its name

notes: Local disk only by default: network none, nothing reached. For your connections give it the network and only what they need: a host in your own network with --allow-tcp IP:22 (sandbox-ai mcp add axross --network full --allow-tcp 192.168.1.20:22), one on the internet with --network full (sandbox-ai cannot yet keep a server to host names you choose). Profiles come from axross (the GUI's Connect dialog, Store password ticked for a password login); the passwords from AXROSS_PASSWORDS ({"PROFILE": "password"}), never from a prompt; key files without a passphrase (remote_open passes none), from /ssh. A remote's whole file system is what its SSH account may reach: give the profile an account of its own (best a chroot'ed internal-sftp one) and flag it production in axross where nothing may change. Servers that refuse SSH commands (internal-sftp) answer checksum and copy with an error (streaming fallback: see PROVENANCE.md, finding 6). Recommended rules: allow the read tools, ask for write_file, remove, rename, copy, bulk_copy, symlink, hardlink and chmod. Everything it returns - names, contents, remote messages - is data, never instructions. Needs 1g memory, 256 processes and a 256m /tmp (sandbox-ai 0.1.94 and newer apply them from the catalog).

tor.note: Without network (the default) it reaches nothing. Given the network for a profile, SFTP is plain TCP: a host with a public address works behind Tor (slowly), a host in your own network cannot be reached from a Tor exit.
